item.title: The Almanac 0.4.4
item.description:
• A calmer Settings › Memory. Your name and what you mostly ask about sit at the top, under the Use memory switch. Below them, your memories are two quiet lists with an "＋ Add" at the end of each, and "Forget everything…" is in the footer.
  • Click anywhere else to stop editing a memory: what you typed is saved. Rows line up and keep their size when you start or stop editing, so nothing jumps.
  • If an edit can't be saved (it's too long, say), clicking away keeps your typing and marks the row "Not saved" until you fix or discard it; quitting discards it. Clearing a memory's text puts the old text back; to remove a memory, use Forget or ⌫, and ⌘Z brings it back.
  • In the welcome, the choices now look like the replies they become, on the right, and a choice only shows it's selected once you move with Tab or the arrow keys. Return still picks Yes.

item.title: The Almanac 0.4.3
item.description:
• The Almanac can remember things about you. Say "Remember that I'm vegetarian" or "Remember that I like short answers" in a chat, and it's saved, with Undo.
  • How you like answers (length, units, tone) shapes every answer except health ones; if you save more than eight, the newest eight are used. Facts about you and your world are used only when a question touches them: the words they back get a dotted underline, and Sources lists them as "Your memory", so you can tell them from the library.
  • When you mention something worth keeping, a "Remember …?" line can appear under the answer. Nothing is saved unless you click it.
  • Settings › Memory replaces Settings › You: see, edit or forget anything, pause memory, or Forget Everything (your name and interest stay). Saying "Forget that…" in a chat works too.
  • "Don't use memory" in the "Searching:" menu gives a chat a clean slate.
  • Health answers are still the reference text word for word. If you've told the Almanac about an allergy that matters, a line above the quotes reminds you, in your own words.
  • Your memory stays on this Mac.

item.title: The Almanac 0.4.2
item.description:
• A warmer voice. Answers read more like a knowledgeable friend and get to the point, without filler like "It's worth noting that" or "Great question!" to start a sentence.
  • The odd emoji: in greetings, quick replies and answers from what the Almanac knows, and now and then on the line that introduces a list in a library answer. Never in a part of an answer that cites a source.
  • The Almanac uses your name from time to time.
  • Health answers are unchanged: the reference text word for word, with no added voice, name or emoji.

item.title: The Almanac 0.4.1
item.description:
• Your messages now sit in a bubble on the right, so it's easy to tell what you said from what the Almanac answered. The welcome chat looks the same way.
  • A cleaner sidebar: one spacing for every row, chats grouped by date, and your sources (the library and your folders) at the bottom with a "+" to add a folder.
  • Your name sits at the bottom of the sidebar and opens Settings. Change your name, or the example questions a new chat suggests, in Settings › You. A short line appears under it only when something needs fixing.
  • Clicking a folder in the sidebar now opens it in Settings › Sources (instead of starting a chat), where you can rename it, show it in Finder, index it again or remove it. Right-click a folder for the same choices. To search just one folder, use "Searching:" above the chat.
  • When your folders cover a question, answers lead with your files. A library page that only shares a name with your question no longer gets into the answer.
  • When nothing in your library or folders covers a question, the Almanac now answers from what it knows straight away, and says so. If that answer stops partway, it says the answer was cut off. Health questions still get only quoted text.
  • "How's your day?" and similar small talk get a reply instead of a library search.
  • While it works, the line beside the infinity says what it's doing: what it's searching, what it's reading and how many sources it's writing from.
  • A finer, engraved infinity mark, in the app, the opening and the icon.
  • An open article no longer jumps back to the quoted passage while you scroll it, and text no longer slides under the top of the window as you scroll.

item.title: The Almanac 0.4.0
item.description:
• Your folders: point the Almanac at folders on your Mac, like notes or a project, and ask questions about them. It reads text, Markdown, code and PDF files. Add a folder from "+ Add folder…" in the sidebar or in Settings › Sources.
  • Answers from your folders cite the file and the lines (or pages, for PDFs). Click a source to open the file.
  • "Searching:" above the chat picks what a conversation searches: everything, just the library, or one folder. Click a folder in the sidebar to start a chat about it.
  • Folders stay up to date as files change. Some files are skipped: anything your .gitignore excludes, files that look like passwords or keys, files over 2 MB (PDFs included), images, audio and video, and Word, Pages and other office documents. Shortcuts to other files or folders aren't followed, and a folder can hold up to 20,000 files.
  • Your files are never changed. Removing a folder only removes the Almanac's index of it.

item.title: The Almanac 0.3.0
item.description:
• More conversational answers: a direct answer first, then the details in short, easy-to-read points.
  • Follow-up questions stay on topic. Ask "why?" or "tell me more" and the Almanac picks up where you left off.
  • Suggested follow-up questions can appear under the latest answer. Click one to ask it.
  • When your library only covers part of a question, the answer says what's missing and offers "Answer from what I know".
  • Questions about burning fuel, like "which wood burns best?", and follow-ups that change the subject get a normal answer.
  • If your library has both the full-text and the short Wikipedia packs, the Almanac searches the full-text one.

item.title: The Almanac 0.2.0
item.description:
• A new welcome for new users: a short chat, then a new opening where a line lifts into the Almanac's infinity. Already set up? See it with Help › Replay welcome.
  • While an answer is on its way, a soft light now glides along the infinity.
  • Delete conversations: right-click one in the sidebar, or File › Delete Conversation… (⌘⌫). Deleted conversations go to the Trash.
  • Closing the window no longer quits the Almanac. It stays in the Dock; click the Dock icon or press ⌘0 to bring it back.
